items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: that's when I first met Jo Jones.

ctx.x: Teddy was writing, too, wasn't he?

Yeah. Teddy, Jonesy, Chuck Lawless(?), Leonard Day... It was a good band. We'd take turns on sleeping. Cats would write all night, then we'd rehearse and...all day. And we (?) that we was ready. Didn't do any rehearsing.
Never got to make any records, huh?

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: We did with Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge.

ctx.x: Hey, you and I made that record.
We did with Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge.
We want to pull that out and we'll take an intermission.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: He's playing with Roy Budd Johnson thing.

ctx.x: Eddie Locke - he's a great drummer -

He's playing with Roy Budd Johnson thing. I used to sit down and tell them, "You're going to play with Earl Hines. You're going to play with Teddy Wilson. You're going to play with Dorothy Donegan. You're going to play with this. You're going to Newport. You're going to Europe." "I am?" I'd say, "Sure you are." "When?" I'd say, "You'll find out." So they found out. I had to tell them now, you see. You know how difficult it is to have a group that's going to stay together for 4 or 5 years, with economic situation…
Let's take a little break... and wet our throats a little here.
